name: What AI Is, in Plain Terms
title: What AI Is, in Plain Terms
answer: Artificial intelligence is software that learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses them to make a guess. Schools meet two kinds: predictive AI, which estimates what is likely and produces numbers, lists or flags, and generative AI, which produces new content such as text, plans, translations or images. The key point is that generative tools are built to sound right, not to be right, and they give no warning when the two come apart.

crumbs.name: What AI Can and Cannot Do

sections.body: This idea explains AI in plain terms so that everyone in a school shares the same basic understanding. AI is software that learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses those patterns to make a guess, and everything else in the book is a variation on that single trick. The idea solves a problem of confusion, because schools actually meet two different kinds of AI and it helps to keep them apart. Predictive AI looks at data and estimates what is likely, answering questions about attendance, bus routes or cafeteria demand, and it produces a number, a list or a flag. Generative AI produces new content such as a paragraph, a lesson plan, a translated letter, a picture or a spoken reply, and tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Claude belong in this group.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, the distinction shows up in how each tool is used and trusted. Predictive AI has been part of school operations for years, often without anyone calling it AI, and it supports decisions such as which students may miss too many days, which bus routes can be combined, or how many lunches to prepare on Friday. Generative AI is used to draft and create, for example a paragraph, a lesson plan, a translated letter, a picture or a spoken reply, and it works by predicting which words usually come next rather than looking an answer up. The text does not give grade band examples, so the practical guidance applies across year groups: staff and students should know which kind of tool they are using and what kind of output to expect from it. The central habit to build is checking generative output, because the tool writes the answer that fits the pattern best and does not know whether what it wrote is true.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no study, figure or finding for this idea, so it rests on practice and explanation rather than research. Its claims are descriptive: AI is software that learns patterns from large amounts of data and uses them to make a guess, predictive AI produces a number, a list or a flag, and generative AI is trained on enormous amounts of text and learns to predict which words usually come next. The text also states that schools have used predictive tools for years, often without calling them AI, which is presented as background rather than as evidence from a study. The one point the chapter stresses above all others is that a generative tool is built to sound right, that sounding right and being right usually line up, and that sometimes they do not, with no warning from the tool when they split.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits and risks in the text centre on truth and on human judgement. A generative AI tool does not look the answer up the way a librarian would, and it does not know whether what it wrote is true, so a person must decide whether the output is accurate before it is used. The tool is built to sound right, and although sounding right and being right usually line up, sometimes they do not, and the tool gives no warning when they split, which places the responsibility for catching errors on the reader. Predictive tools also produce estimates rather than certainties, since they estimate what is likely, so the decisions that follow from a number, a list or a flag stay with people. The text does not set out specific rules, laws or policies, so these guardrails describe practice and the judgement that remains with staff, leaders and families.
